resources.string: Maps the HiBreak Pro side keys to custom functions
SideKeys intercepts the hardware side keys and runs the actions you choose (e.g. Google Assistant, Google Wallet or launching an app). The service does not read screen content and collects no data.

To remap the side keys, SideKeys must be enabled as an accessibility service. Tap below and enable "SideKeys Button Mapper".\n\nIf the toggle is blocked ("Restricted setting"): open SideKeys app info → menu (⋮) → "Allow restricted settings" — Android requires this for sideloaded apps.
No key assigned yet. Tap "Assign key" and then press one of the side keys of your HiBreak Pro.
The mapping for "%1$s" will be removed. The key gets its original function back.
Now press the side key you want to assign
Works with both extra keys of the HiBreak Pro — and with other hardware keys too.
Note: capturing already works now, but for the key to react system-wide the accessibility service must be enabled.
Choose an action for each press type. Use ▶ to test the action immediately.
Service not active — please enable the accessibility service first.
For special functions, e.g. Bigme-specific settings. Provide at least an action or a component.
Note: if a double press is assigned, the single press only fires after this window has passed.
The HiBreak Pro side keys sometimes fire twice. Presses arriving faster than this interval are ignored.

• If a side key never arrives: set its assignment to "None" in Bigme settings under "Custom key" so SideKeys receives it.\n\n• Bigme/MediaTek "DuraSpeed" aggressively kills background apps. If the service stops, disable DuraSpeed (via ADB: settings put global setting.duraspeed.enabled 0) and exempt SideKeys from battery optimization.
No assistant found. Is the Google Assistant installed?
App not found — has it been uninstalled?
This action requires Android 9 or newer.
No flashlight found on this device.
The action could not be executed.
Please allow SideKeys to access Do Not Disturb and try again.
